title: บันทึกแพตช์ speaks Thai and shows the newest build, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.16 — บันทึกแพตช์ speaks Thai and shows the newest build, deployed to production. The page rendered one long English paragraph per release and its baked JSON stopped at 1.1.13, so the owner saw English and no sign of 1.1.14/1.1.15. Every release now has an authored Thai entry (src/data/patch-notes-th.json, keyed by BUILD_ID) split into ปัญหา / สิ่งที่เปลี่ยน / ตรวจสอบแล้ว / หมายเหตุ, dates read 5 พ.ย. 2569, and the live card carries the newest release's detail instead of only its title. That layer is hand-written, so P6/P7 make a missing (or orphaned) Thai entry a red build rather than English on a Thai panel. Verified on the served chunk page-47d1d3887e109a18.js (200, 56,667 bytes): สิ่งที่เปลี่ยน, ตรวจสอบแล้ว and the newest Thai titles are all present. Live: 1.1.16 / #405 / C-hiNzGj4ALNiP-mK3I9T / de168e7. The page cannot list its own row yet — a bundle is always baked before the row that describes it exists — so it names the running build and shows the previous release under a caption saying whose detail it is.

title: The token travels as a curl config, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.15 — the token travels as a curl config, deployed to production. 1.1.14 wrote the bare token intending -H x-cron-token:$(cat …), and the first live run taught the real constraint: Plesk's scheduler kills any command containing $ — both the inline substitution and a T=$(cat …) assignment ended error in under a second with empty output, while the identical command without $ ran fine. The file is now a curl config (header = "x-cron-token: …", 0600) read with -K, so the task needs no substitution and no quoting. Task 254 (*/10 * * * *, Active) drives the three sweeps; its first run authenticated and returned {"ok":true,"scanned":2,"expired":2,"timeoutMinutes":30}, expiring the two audit orders (NK-2026-000190, -000191) that had been waiting since morning. Three hours later the evidence file had advanced on its own (cutoff 07:20Z → 10:10Z, ~18 fires), and cron-curl.conf had been rewritten at 10:45Z when Passenger respawned the app — so both the cadence and the boot path hold without attention. -K was checked against the live endpoint first with a dummy token (401, not 503), so the header really was sent. Live: 1.1.15 / #402 / Cvm6k6VOEzORNV_BiJ7QN / a9c9472.

title: The boot hands the sweep token to Plesk, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.14 — the boot hands the sweep token to Plesk, deployed to production. Plesk's scheduler runs outside the Node process, so it can never see NK_CRON_SECRET, and its task field renders secrets as plain text on a public repo — which is why the sweeps were still riding GitHub's 4–5 runs a day. server.js now mirrors the secret to tmp/cron-curl.conf (0600) at boot, from the same env it already injects, so nobody has to copy a secret between panels. Verified live: the file is -rw------- nongka psacln, and everything under /tmp/ answers 403 over HTTPS (Plesk blocks the path whether or not a file exists there, so that 403 is not evidence of the file — the listing is). Live: 1.1.14 / #401 / Opp1E9sP7OPnK69ZOE-eU / 7a67438, health database: ok.

title: A hold now expires on its own clock, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.13 — a hold now expires on its own clock, deployed to production. Auditing 1.1.12 found order NK-2026-000190 still holding a unit 100 minutes after its 30-minute window: the GitHub schedule meant to tick every 10 minutes had run at 01:51Z and not since, and the previous day had four runs. A hold that waits for that tick is a hold of unknown length, so the hold query now filters order.createdAt > now − payment window, reading the same SiteSetting the sweep reads; the sweep still flips the row to expired. Live A/B on the 2-unit variant: under 1.1.12 the stale hold blocked a qty-2 order; after this deploy the same request created NK-2026-000191, and the next qty-1 request returned 409 OUT_OF_STOCK from the fresh hold. Live: 1.1.13 / #398 / Yyc-JBjGfuh2D6Xjfz8YT / c9f08fd, health database: ok. The schedule behind the *status* flip was measured the same day over 12 runs: 4–5 a day, 3–5 hours apart, all green — what that does and does not cost is written up in production-health-monitoring.md §3b.

title: An expired order can still be paid, and the lookup cap now counts misses, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.12 — an expired order can still be paid, and the lookup cap now counts misses, deployed to production. A customer who transferred at minute 29 and uploaded the slip at minute 31 got 409 from a shop already holding their money: the claim CAS and both slip guards demanded exactly pending_payment. All three now accept expired, and a unit that was resold meanwhile still parks as pending_manual_fulfilment (existing path, no new code). The per-email lookup bucket was peeked and consumed only on a match, so the guessing it exists to stop never spent it — it now counts every attempt at 10/15 min, which also lets ten junk requests lock one address's lookup for 15 minutes (that customer keeps the order link in their email). Also deletes 1,587 lines of never-imported modules — coupon/loyalty/category APIs, three service wrappers, the cart shell, mega menu, progress ring, CSV parser and a duplicate slug helper — plus the one test that kept the parser alive, and the stock-parser row/section it needed in docs/quality-gates.md. Live: 1.1.12 / #397 / d18M2Uu2sTMnqp7_i96lj / 0359c45; lookup 10×404 then 429; the checkout copy in the deployed chunk reads "ประมาณ 30 นาที" (the old "สูงสุด" is gone).

title: The last code can no longer be sold twice, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.11 — the last code can no longer be sold twice, deployed to production. The 5 Nov audit found the money path careful right up to its edges: an unpaid order held nothing (stock checked at creation, code taken at confirmation), so two customers could each buy the last unit, both transfer, and the second slip would verify against stock already gone — parked for a manual refund. createOrderInner now subtracts what pending_payment orders already hold, inside the same Serializable transaction as the insert, and the 30-minute sweep is the release (derived, no new column, no stock write). Live proof: with 2 units and 1 held, a second order for 2 returned 409 OUT_OF_STOCK and created nothing. Guest /orders/lookup, which hands back the UUID that opens a page of delivered codes, now has per-IP (10/15min) and per-email (5/15min, peeked so a stranger cannot spend a victim's quota) buckets — live: 10×404 then 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Also deletes 696 lines of mock reservation/delivery code that production never ran. Live: 1.1.11 / #393 / Of0v841HVtlWHuQNQx9lE / 55b56ba, health database: ok.

title: The panel now names the build that is actually serving, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.10 — the panel now names the build that is actually serving, deployed to production. 1.1.9's page was honest about its list but not about "latest": its data is baked into the bundle, so the first build showed "ล่าสุด 1.1.8" while 1.1.9 was live (proven in the real panel). The top card now reads the running build through useRelease() — the module that already owns the panel's single cached /api/v1/version request, enforced by tests/release-badge.test.ts; the first attempt used its own fetch and that gate went red, so it was rewritten onto the shared hook. When the running build has no log row the card says so instead of presenting an older release as current. Live: /api/v1/version → 1.1.10 / #391 / ANp_hPzY4PUJ9hbRpy0Iq / 164677e; the page shows "build ที่ให้บริการอยู่ตอนนี้ v1.1.10" and 10 logged releases newest-first.

title: The panel can show what shipped, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.9 — the panel can show what shipped, deployed to production. The owner was asking for release history every time, because the only record lived in this file. New page /management/patch-notes (การดูแลระบบ → บันทึกแพตช์, settings:read) lists every build that reached production — version, date, BUILD_ID, commit, what changed — and its data is generated, not copied: scripts/patch-notes.mjs (npm run patch-notes) parses this deploy-log table into src/data/patch-notes.json, so the page can only show what the runbook actually recorded, and rows that shipped no code (DB cleanups, secret rotations) stay out. tests/patch-notes.test.ts P1–P5 fails when the log is edited without regenerating — proven by inserting a fake Nov 5 row, watching P1 go red (expected [1.1.8…] to deeply equal [1.1.9…]), then restoring the log. Two parser defects surfaced during the build and were fixed before shipping: dates drifted one day back (local UTC+7 midnight → previous day in UTC) and titles lost their capital. Live: /api/v1/version → 1.1.9 / #390 / um9kUzepqJodcpCTAAy6U / dd145cc; the page renders 9 rows newest-first with the newest detail expanded.

title: /management is a door again, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.8 — /management is a door again, deployed to production. The audit on 1.1.7 found that /management/ answered 308 → /management and /management answered 404: app/management/ had layout.tsx and every sub-route but no root page, while the spec calls that URL the admin entry (02-user-flow "Entry: /management/ → redirect to /management/login/", 03-IA "/management/ … Admin Dashboard"). The fix is a redirect-only page to /management/login, which already owns the auth decision and hands a live session to the dashboard, so there is still exactly one gate. tests/admin-nav-sections.test.ts now lists /management with login and dev-seed as a deliberate non-menu page, and tests/management-entry.test.ts (M1–M4) holds the redirect, the absence of admin markup, and the login page's authenticated bounce. Live: /api/v1/version → 1.1.8 / #388 / asv940_oIRI6rFKVRgObZ / d71dc88, health database: ok with uptime 81 s. /management → 200 and lands on /management/login in a clean browser (email + password + remember + submit, x-robots-tag: noindex); /management/ still 308s into it; with a live admin session the same navigation ends on /management/dashboard, so "entry, or dashboard when authenticated" is proven both ways. Re-audit on the new build: guest /management/orders and /management/settings still return the empty shell (0 order numbers, 0 emails), guest admin APIs 401 with 405 on a wrong method, manual-info still enabled: true / 199-1-73578-6 / กนกนาถ โรจนวุฒิ, slip-verify still 403 INVALID_UPLOAD_TOKEN for missing / fake / plausible-64-char tokens, /orders/preview still rejects VARIANT_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_QUANTITY (-2, 1.5) and 51 items as CART_TOO_LARGE, security headers present with a CSP nonce, homepage 0 turbopack, product/search/checkout 200. Cleanup Run Now answered CLEANED with .next + .next.old in place; no rollback was needed.

title: The payment tab can save its bank account again, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.7 — the payment tab can save its bank account again, deployed to production. The header save kept ONE saver slot while the payment tab renders two panels, so PaymentSettings registered second and overwrote ManualTransferSettings — an edited receiver account never left the browser while the button reported success. Panels now register through useSettingsSaver and the page runs every registered saver; a refused save reports its reason. Also carries one shared applyPromotionDiscount (three copies had drifted apart), a MAX_CART_ITEMS = 50 guard on /orders/preview (the 60/min IP rule already covered flood; the caller-controlled array did not), cache() on the two category readers, and the search filter chip. Live: /api/v1/version → 1.1.7 / #386 / IfozWtRR1lZBnFJj_XUQg / 11f9929, health database: ok with uptime 24s (a real restart), products 200, homepage 0 turbopack, CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy all present. Audit on the deployed build: 51 preview items → 400 CART_TOO_LARGE, 1 item → ฿50 and qty 2 → ฿100 (stock and price agree with the product page's เหลือ 2); Thai-slug product 200 in both percent-encoded and raw UTF-8 forms; search ?q=365 returns 2 cards with the query echoed in the heading; /category/workspace 200; cart totals 9×฿1 + ฿50 = ฿59; every guest call to /api/v1/admin/* answers 401 and POST on a GET-only admin route answers 405. Run Now with the canonical 653-char line (task id 250, deactivated, not saved); extract-check.txt and the tarball removed by a second Run Now that answered CLEANED, then the field restored to the deploy one-liner. Open: the settings-tab fix itself needs an admin login to exercise (not done here, the panel is behind auth); production reports vatEnabled: false, so VAT stays switched off; the cart drawer's entrance animation could not be watched because the browser tab was backgrounded (Chromium parks animations at currentTime 0 when visibilityState is hidden), so only its markup and totals were checked.

title: The /search landing now announces its category filter.
detail: 1.1.6 — the /search landing now announces its category filter. Audited on 1.1.5: /search?category=streaming-app filtered the grid correctly but carried no aria-current on any chip, while the navbar's สินค้าทั้งหมด link announced itself as the current page despite pointing at a different view. Fix: the selected chip renders aria-current="page" beside its existing peach active state (and ทั้งหมด is current only without a filter), and /search passes searchCategory through FacebookLayout into FacebookNavbar so the navbar entry stays inert while filtered. Guard tests/search-category-chip.test.ts (C1–C5) + a docs/quality-gates.md row/section (SC). Live proof on the new build: /search?category=streaming-app has exactly one aria-current="page" — the streaming app (19) chip — with work space (3) / Chinese Miniseries (7) inactive and ทั้งหมด unmarked; each drawer destination (workspace 3, streaming-app 19, chinese-miniseries 7) returns 200 with its own chip active; unfiltered /search marks ทั้งหมด. Unchanged behaviours re-checked: product page เหลือ 2, the five preview-order cases (OUT_OF_STOCK at 0 codes, ฿50/฿100 for 2 stock/2 codes, qty3 rejected), /category/streaming-app 200.

detail: 1.1.5 — sellable-stock gate + one-tap drawer, deployed to production. Carries 391c376 (the resolver now counts available GiftCode rows, so a variant sells min(stock, codes) and refuses OUT_OF_STOCK below the quantity; the product page shows the deliverable number) and f322dcd (drawer category rows point at /search?category=<slug> instead of /category/<slug>, so the client gets their one tap to a price; the grouped tile page and its ดูทั้งหมด entry points are untouched). Live: /api/v1/version → 1.1.5 / #377 / WGagTETnKgIY7F02yeydr / b68bbc6, health database: ok with uptime 4.5s (a real restart, not a stale process), products 200, homepage 0 turbopack. Audited on the deployed build: /search?category=streaming-app 19 cards all หมด (genuine — every streaming variant is 0 stock / 0 codes); microsoft-365-30-วัน-ytbr shows เหลือ 2 and previews ฿50 (qty 1) / ฿100 (qty 2); qty 3 and both 0-code variants answer OUT_OF_STOCK; drawer at 390px lists workspace / streaming-app / Chinese Miniseries with /search?category= hrefs and the grouped /category/streaming-app still 200. title: Real public origin + honest drawer categories, deployed to production.
detail: 1.1.4 — real public origin + honest drawer categories, deployed to production. Carries 1.1.3 (a126c25, 46CiMm7RsXYLfD_rc-bNe) and the fixes stacked on it: (a) publicOrigin() now treats a loopback NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL as unset and falls back to https://nongkatistore.com, so the origin inlined at build time can no longer ship localhost; (b) the drawer's category fetch no longer caches a 500 as an empty list, shows skeleton rows while in flight and retries on the next open. Live: /api/v1/version → 1.1.4 / #373 / 4e9dcbf, health database: ok; homepage and the Thai-slug product microsoft-365-30-วัน-ytbr 200; sitemap has 0 localhost and emits https://nongkatistore.com/product/microsoft-365-30-%E0%B8%A7…; that product's canonical and og:url match; robots.txt sitemap points at the real domain; drawer verified at 390px — forced 500 shows the "โหลดหมวดหมู่ไม่สำเร็จ" line with 0 dead links, closing and reopening refetches and renders the three real categories, a cached reopen fires 0 requests. Run Now with a pinned TARBID guard (5 s), extract-check.txt read then deleted; task left unsaved with the canonical 653-char line.

title: Version-endpoint fix + /search dropdown fix — deployed to production.
detail: Version-endpoint fix + /search dropdown fix — deployed to production. Also carries the TOTP generator fix, navbar popover portals, and the credential-file ignore. Post-deploy, /api/v1/version returns a buildId read from .next/BUILD_ID on disk and it reports the real deployed build; gitSha still echoes the stale Infisical value (2ee2ae7) and is no longer the verification signal. deploy-rollback was repointed to the previous bundle (gUxcV6SEGUgIp6nFJf8hR) BEFORE the force-push, so rollback stayed available. Pre-publish secret scan: unpacked the bundle and searched every file for the literal values of NK_JWT_SECRET, NK_GIFT_CODE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_DIRECT_URL (plus the postgres user and password substrings) — none present, no .env* staged. The 14 grep hits were variable NAMES (process.env["NK_GIFT_CODE_ENCRYPTION_KEY"]), not values. Live verification: health healthy/database: ok with uptime 13s (confirming a real restart, not a stale process), /, /search, /management/login, /account/login, /api/v1/products all 200, 0 turbopack leaks. Browser-checked on the deployed build at 740x420: the search list is portaled, position: fixed, 691px — exactly the search bar's width and left edge, fully inside the viewport with all 6 options hit-testable (it previously hung 177px past the fold, stranding the last two); clicking the previously-unreachable last option navigates. All three navbar popovers re-checked for regression: portaled, fixed, zero clipping ancestors, fully visible (notifications 320x322 at top=60). Plesk: extract ran via Run Now with no task saved; extract-check.txt deleted; no probe*/restart-watch*/deploy-bundle residue in the docroot.

title: Navbar layout fix — deployed to production.
detail: Navbar layout fix — deployed to production. Fix: header nav links were crushed to one Thai glyph per line between ~768–1150px because the centre nav was a plain flex child with no shrink-0, so it absorbed the whole width deficit and Thai broke *between glyphs*. Added shrink-0 to nav + links, whitespace-nowrap, min-w-0/flex-1 on the search field, moved the nav breakpoint md: → xl: (1280px), and added the two missing drawer links (แนะนำ, รายการโปรด). 4 new gates in tests/navbar-layout-gates.test.ts; full suite 349 ✓. Live after deploy: nav links 41px single-line at 1280px, nav display:none below xl, search 224×21px at 768/900px, no horizontal overflow at any width; health database: ok, products 200, homepage 0 turbopack. Deploy was blocked for ~2 days by a Plesk quoting bug, not by the network — see deploy-hostatom-manual.md pitfalls. Infisical GIT_SHA was stale at 13bdf58 and has since been corrected to 2ee2ae7… (a human-edited Infisical value, not a code change); /api/v1/version now reports the live commit.
